Core: Obstetrics, Paediatrics, Surgery and First Aid

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The co-existence of high youth unemployment alongside widespread corporate talent shortages reveals a deep structural mismatch between formal educational curricula and the fast-evolving needs of the modern labor market. Academic institutions remain stubbornly tethered to legacy rote-learning systems that prioritize theoretical memorization over practical, dynamic problem-solving and technical fluency. As industrial sectors rapidly transform through automation, data analytics, and green engineering, graduates enter the workforce with obsolete skill sets, rendering them functionally unemployable despite holding formal degrees. Resolving this structural employment bottleneck requires a fundamental overhaul of vocational training, moving away from low-tier manual training toward high-value technical and cognitive skill development. This transformation requires deep institutional partnerships between universities and industries, ensuring that apprenticeships, real-world project learning, and adaptive digital skills are deeply integrated into curricula. Youth employment strategies must look beyond simply increasing graduation rates, focusing instead on building a highly agile, continuously upskilling workforce capable of navigating continuous industrial disruption.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Human skin maintains its health and smoothness by means of a fatty substance called sebum, secreted by millions of glands located near the roots of hair. This oily substance oozes to the skin and forms a protective mixture with sweat, to keep our skin moist and pliable. In very cold weather the sebum congeals and does not come to the surface of the skin; as a result, the skin becomes dry and chapped. Over-production or under-production of sebum causes excessively oily skin or excessively dry skin. During adolescence there is a rapid increase in sebum production causing skin eruptions. But as we grow older, sebum production decreases, causing dry skin, wrinkles and lack of elasticity. Although all skins seem to look alike, our skin is particularly our own, so that our fingerprint patterns are unique and can never be found duplicated in any other skin pattern. Similarly, when there is a skin transplant, the skin is taken from another part of the same body, otherwise the body is liable to reject it.

questions.q: The simultaneous existence of youth unemployment and corporate talent shortages is, according to the author, proof of:
opts: A structural mismatch between curricula and market needs.
The failure of job portals to track vacancies.
A drop in the number of students taking degrees.
Companies refusing to pay fair wages.
questions.why: Detail: the first sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Traditional academic institutions are criticized for prioritizing:
opts: Rote learning and theoretical memorization over practical problem-solving.
questions.why: Detail: the second sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, why are many degree holders "functionally unemployable"?
opts: They lack capital to start businesses.
Universities have replaced theory with apprenticeships.
Automation has removed all human jobs.
They graduate with obsolete skills that do not match industry needs.
questions.why: Detail: the third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: To resolve the employment bottleneck, vocational training must:
opts: Shift toward high-value technical and cognitive skills.
Focus only on low-tier manual skills.
Be cut off from industry input.
Spend more time on rote learning.
questions.why: Detail: the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The ultimate goal of youth employment strategies should be to:
opts: Maximise graduation numbers without changing curricula.
Build an agile, continuously upskilling workforce.
Subsidise firms that hire untrained graduates.
questions.why: Main idea: the last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The discussion of sebum in the passage is relevant because sebum is
opts: an oily substance that oozes to the skin
secreted at the roots of hair
protective of the health of human skin
questions.why: Main idea: skin 'maintains its health and smoothness by means of' sebum. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Programme Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which of the following is an INACCURATE statement about human skin, according to the passage?
opts: In a skin transplant the donor and recipient are usually the same person
Excess sebum in adolescence causes skin eruptions
questions.why: The passage says skins only 'seem to look alike'; each skin is 'particularly our own'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Programme Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which word in the passage means moving tissue from one site to another?
questions.why: Vocabulary from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Programme Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: According to the passage, the cause of loss of elasticity of the skin in older people is
questions.why: Detail: 'as we grow older, sebum production decreases, causing dry skin, wrinkles and lack of elasticity'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Programme Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: In very cold weather the skin becomes dry and chapped because
opts: sebum congeals and does not reach the surface
the glands near the hair roots are damaged
questions.why: Detail: the third sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Programme Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “I wish I ______ the answer to your question.”
questions.why: 'Wish' about the present takes the past form (subjunctive). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Find the error: “He has been living in Panaji for 2019.”
questions.why: Use 'since' with a point of time (2019); 'for' with a period (five years). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “I am tired.”
opts: He said that he was tired.
He said that I was tired.
He said that he is tired.
He said that he had been tired yesterday.
questions.why: Reporting verb in the past: am → was; I → he. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the camp.”
questions.why: First conditional: if + present, will + verb. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the conjunction relationship: “Although he was ill, he attended office.”
questions.why: 'Although' introduces a contrast (concession). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

Under VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA in 2026, each rural household is guaranteed how many days of wage work a year?
questions.why: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days.

questions.q: India won the Women's T20 Asia Cup 2026. How many times has India won the women's Asia Cup?
questions.why: Shafali Verma was Player of the Tournament. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Who won the Best Young Player award at the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.why: July 2026.

questions.q: World Patient Safety Day is observed on:
questions.why: The 2026 theme focused on safe care for noncommunicable diseases.

questions.q: Goa's highest peak is:
questions.why: In the Sahyadri, Sattari–Sanguem.

questions.q: INS Mahendragiri, the sixth Project 17A frigate commissioned in July 2026, was built by:
questions.why: July 2026.

questions.q: SEBI's 'Credit Risk-o-Meter' (2026) is meant to assess the credit risk of:
The southwest monsoon reached Kerala in 2026 on:
questions.why: The normal onset date is 1 June.

questions.q: Varsha Ashok Aglawe made history in August 2026 when she became the first woman to head the:
questions.why: GSI, founded 1851, is headquartered in Kolkata.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 3, 6, 18, 72, 360, ?
questions.why: The multipliers are 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6: 360 x 6 = 2160.

questions.q: If A = 2, B = 4, C = 6 and so on, what is the value of G + O + A?
Book is to library as painting is to:
questions.why: Books are kept and shown in a library; paintings in a gallery.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: The first three are four-sided figures. A triangle has three sides.

questions.q: X and Y are husband and wife. Z is their daughter and W is their son. V is W's son. How is X related to V?
questions.why: X is the father of W, and W is the father of V, so X is V's grandfather.

questions.q: A man leaves his house, walks 10 m east, turns right and walks 5 m, then turns right again and walks 10 m. Where is he in relation to his house?
questions.why: He goes 10 m east, 5 m south and 10 m back west, ending 5 m south of the house.

questions.q: The average age of 30 students is 15 years. Including the teacher, the average rises by 1. What is the teacher's age?
Find the compound interest on ₹1,600 at 10% a year for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.why: 1600 × 1.21 = 1936; interest 336. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Four boxes each hold the same number of sweets and carry these labels: 'Five or Six', 'Seven or Eight', 'Six or Seven', 'Seven or Five'. Only one label is correct. How many sweets are in each box?
questions.why: Five, six and seven each make two labels true. Eight makes only 'Seven or Eight' true. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.why: The others are a substance and what holds it; a nib is part of a pen. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Naegele's rule estimates the expected date of delivery by adding to the first day of the last menstrual period:
questions.why: Equivalent to 280 days.

questions.q: Pre-eclampsia is defined as hypertension after 20 weeks of pregnancy with:
questions.why: With convulsions it becomes eclampsia.

questions.q: Gestational diabetes is screened for in India using:
opts: a 75 g oral glucose test (single step, DIPSI)
questions.why: Two-hour value of 140 mg/dL or more.

questions.q: The second stage of labour is from:
opts: onset of pains to full dilatation
delivery of the baby to delivery of the placenta
full dilatation of the cervix to delivery of the baby
questions.why: Third stage ends with expulsion of the placenta.

questions.q: Painful menstruation with no pelvic pathology, starting soon after menarche, is called:
questions.why: Secondary dysmenorrhoea has a cause such as endometriosis.

questions.q: Irregular cycles, hirsutism, acne and multiple ovarian follicles on ultrasound suggest:
questions.why: Rotterdam criteria.

questions.q: The commonest benign tumour of the uterus is:
questions.why: Smooth-muscle tumour.

questions.q: A baby typically sits without support at about:
questions.why: Walks alone around 12–15 months.

questions.q: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life is:
questions.why: Physiological jaundice appears after 24 hours.

questions.q: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first:
questions.why: WHO and Indian guidelines.

questions.q: Rickets results from deficiency of:
questions.why: Bowing of legs, rachitic rosary.

questions.q: Under India's Universal Immunisation Programme, BCG is given:
questions.why: With OPV-0 and hepatitis B birth dose.

questions.q: A child with difficult dentition, greenish diarrhoea, and who wants to be carried constantly calls for:
questions.why: Chamomilla's irritability during teething.

questions.q: The 'rule of nines' is used to estimate:
opts: the percentage of body surface area burnt
the severity of a head injury
questions.why: Head 9%, each arm 9%, each leg 18%, trunk 36%, perineum 1%.

questions.q: The commonest type of shock after trauma is:
questions.why: From blood loss.

questions.q: A collection of pus in a cavity lined by granulation tissue is called:
questions.why: Treated by drainage.

questions.q: A Colles' fracture is a fracture of the:
questions.why: From a fall on the outstretched hand.

questions.q: Infection of bone, commonly by Staphylococcus aureus, is called:
questions.why: Usually affects the metaphysis in children.

questions.q: Pain and stiffness worse on beginning to move and better with continued motion, as in sprains or spondylosis, call for:
questions.why: Rhus tox: better from continued motion.

questions.q: Raised intraocular pressure with optic nerve damage is called:
questions.why: Leads to field loss.

questions.q: Ear pain in a child after a cold, with a red, bulging eardrum, suggests:
questions.why: Middle ear infection.

questions.q: For bruises, falls and blunt injuries with a sore, bruised feeling, the first remedy is:
questions.why: Arnica for blunt trauma.

questions.q: For injury to nerve-rich parts such as crushed fingertips, with shooting pains along the nerve, use:
questions.why: Hypericum is the remedy for nerve injuries.

questions.q: Calendula is mainly used externally to:
opts: promote healing of lacerated wounds and prevent suppuration
questions.why: Calendula lotion or tincture for wounds.

questions.q: First aid for a snakebite includes:
opts: immobilising the limb and transporting quickly to a hospital with anti-snake venom
questions.why: Cutting, sucking and tight tourniquets are no longer advised.
